normal.filenameResolution: The upstream filename says 783m; the catalog and actual GeoTIFF geotransform establish 802.85145591739 m/pixel.
normal.coordinates: North up; center longitude 0, positive raster easting. Roll the 180 E left edge by half a width to 0–360 E, never mirror. USGS already applied the stated 4.5-degree westward IAU correction; do not apply it again.

enhanced.coordinates: North up, 0 E left edge. The bright trailing hemisphere is centered near 90 E; dark Cassini Regio is centered near 270 E. Compared matching crater/ridge and boundary patterns with the rolled monochrome source.
enhanced.processing: Published calibration, registration and photometric correction by Paul Schenk. Preserve intrinsic hemisphere albedo and color, including very dark pixels. No new brightness matching or photographic shadow removal.

shape.limitations: Spherical rendering approximation. Iapetus has an oblate figure and a prominent equatorial ridge; the observed ridge remains in the imagery, not in displaced geometry.

terrain.reason: No directly downloadable qualified height raster found. The current PDS Cassini SPC archive has no Iapetus bundle; the 2025 author abstract describes Iapetus as forthcoming. The USGS foundational inventory lists older Cassini stereo topography as unreleased. Do not derive elevation from image brightness.

facts.albedo: NASA reports leading hemisphere albedo 0.03–0.05 versus trailing 0.5–0.6. The contrast is physical surface reflectivity, not no-data.
facts.atmosphere: No visible atmosphere layer is included.
